Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.The study of ancient civilisations provides valuable insights into human history, offering a window into the lives of people who lived thousands of years ago. Archaeological discoveries have shed light on the daily lives and customs of ancient peoples, revealing how they lived, worked and interacted with their environment. These findings help us understand the development of cultures and societies, showing us the evolution of human civilisation over time. For instance, the excavation of ancient cities has uncovered artifacts such as tools, pottery and inscriptions that tell us about the technological advancements, trade practices and social structures of these societies.However, interpreting these artifacts can be challenging due to limited information. Often, archaeologists must piece together incomplete records and fragmented objects to form a coherent picture of the past. This process requires a great deal of expertise and often involves making educated guesses based on the available evidence. The context in which an artifact is found can significantly influence its interpretation, and without a complete understanding of this context, our conclusions may be tentative or subject to revision.Ongoing research and technological advances continue to reveal new aspects of ancient civilisations. Modern techniques such as radiocarbon dating, DNA analysis and remote sensing have revolutionised the field of archaeology, allowing researchers to obtain more precise and detailed information about ancient peoples and their environments.What types of artifacts are commonly discovered in ancient cities?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (Tools, pottery, and inscriptions) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.Critical theory of technology is a political theory of modernity with a normative dimension. It comes from a tradition extending from Marx to Foucault and Habermas which says that advances in the formal claims of human rights take centre stage. Marx attributed this trajectory to the capitalist rationalisation of production. It is prevalent in every modern political system. This trajectory arose from the problems of control over a disempowered and deskilled labour force; but everywhere it is organised — be it Foucault's prisons or Habermas's public sphere — the same pattern prevails. Technological design is shaped by this pattern as the material base of a distinctive social order. In accordance with the notion of thought, critical theory of technology regards technologies as an environment rather than as a collection of tools. We are surrounded by technologies that determine our way of life. The  theory builds an approach on the lessons of these histories. In this respect, they are comparable to laws and customs. These institutions said to represent those who live under their sway through privileging certain dimensions of their human nature. Laws of property represent the interest in ownership. Customs like parental authority represent the interest of childhood in safety and growth. Interests, such as these constitute the version of human nature sanctioned by society. The concept of nature suggests an alternative. The reference here is, of course, not to the nature of natural science, but to the lived nature in which we find ourselves and which we are.Which of the following assertions most appropriately sums up the theme of the passage?
options: Certain aspects of human nature, like earning more and more, are given more weight in technological surroundings than in laws and norms.
If viewed as institutions, technology, laws, and customs are similar to each other.
Automobiles are a symbol of the human desire for mobility and spiritual upliftment.
Laws, customs, and technology are similar but different phenomena are applied for them.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (If viewed as institutions, technology, laws, and customs are similar to each other.) है।

Comprehension:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.Urban gardening has emerged as a practical and sustainable solution to the challenges posed by rapid urbanisation. As cities continue to grow, they face mounting issues such as food insecurity, air pollution, declining green spaces, and rising temperatures. Urban gardening, which involves cultivating fruits, vegetables, and herbs in small spaces such as rooftops, balconies, and community gardens, offers a way to counter these problems. It transforms unused or underutilised spaces into productive green areas, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability.In addition to providing fresh and nutritious produce, urban gardening has mental health benefits, reduces the urban heat island effect, and strengthens social bonds among city dwellers. These gardens serve as educational tools, especially for children, by promoting awareness about nutrition, ecology, and biodiversity. Recognising these advantages, local governments and NGOs are increasingly supporting such initiatives through grants, training programs, and policy support. However, urban gardening also faces hurdles like limited space, poor soil quality, water scarcity, and a lack of gardening knowledge among residents. Overcoming these barriers requires community involvement, education, and integration with smart urban planning. Despite these challenges, the growing interest in sustainable living and environmental stewardship suggests that urban gardening will play a vital role in shaping the green cities of the future.What is the tone of the passage?

Comprehension:Read the given passage written by Narayani Ganesh and answer the questions that follow.Work that nourishes the mind, body and soul. Why do we work? Most would say to sustain themselves and their families. While some may love their profession, monetary return remains essential. However, the tragedy begins when work feeds only the body and mind, leaving the soul starved. Prolonged neglect of the soul due to relentless work pressures can be deeply damaging—emotionally, mentally and even physically.The solution lies in finding a creative outlet—something simple, hands-on, and joy-giving that isn’t burdened by deadlines or expectations. Activities like playing an instrument, gardening, painting, embroidery, carpentry or any other hobby that brings peace and fulfillment can nourish the soul. Such pursuits can lead to a profound transformation. They not only provide inner joy but also enhance one’s efficiency, creativity and problem-solving abilities at work. This change improves interpersonal skills and makes the individual more engaged and present in both, professional and personal life.Gradually, instead of wasting time on passive entertainment like mindless scrolling or binge-watching, one starts valuing time and connecting more meaningfully with the world. The mind, body and soul begin to function in harmony, leading to inner joy and outward positivity. This rejuvenation fosters compassion, love and appreciation, replacing complaints with gratitude. Even monotonous tasks become opportunities for innovation.This inner shift mirrors cultural movements like slow food or the resurgence of reading in a screen-dominated age. As John Ruskin said, “The highest reward for a man’s toil is not what he gets for it but what he becomes by it.” Let’s pursue that deeper reward.What is the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'rejuvenation' as used in the passage?

Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Pregnancy is a time of change. As the mother’s womb grows, the baby develops. The final 3 months of pregnancy, known as the third trimester, are a really important time for brain development—but sometimes babies are born early.
The third trimester is especially important for the development of the limbic system. If you have ever seen the movie Inside Out, the limbic system is like the brain’s control centre for emotions. The limbic system is made up of five main parts, the amygdala, hypothalamus, basal ganglia, thalamus and hippocampus, which each help us control and understand our emotions.
Without the limbic system, it would be impossible to stop crying or yelling and we might have no idea why we even started. During the third trimester of pregnancy, every part of the limbic system is developing to help the baby handle their emotions once they are born.
By the end of the third trimester, babies have as many neurons as adults (about 100 billion), even though their brains are only about a quarter of the size! Neurons are brain cells that help the parts of the brain talk to each other.What does the word 'control' most likely mean in the sentence 'the limbic system is like the brain’s control centre for emotions'?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (Regulate or manage) है।

Comprehension:Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.Climate change is one of the most pressing challenges facing the world today. It refers to long-term changes in temperature, precipitation, and weather patterns, largely caused by human activities such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation. These changes have led to more frequent and intense natural disasters like hurricanes, droughts, and floods, affecting millions of people globally. Coastal regions are particularly vulnerable, with rising sea levels threatening communities and ecosystems alike. Scientists agree that reducing greenhouse gas emissions is critical to slowing climate change. Many countries have pledged to shift towards renewable energy sources like solar and wind power to decrease their carbon footprint. This transition not only reduces harmful emissions but also promotes energy independence and green job creation. Additionally, protecting forests and promoting sustainable agriculture can help absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Reforestation efforts and the preservation of biodiversity play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance and reducing carbon levels. The impacts of climate change are not limited to the environment; they also affect economies and public health. Crop failures, water shortages, and increased disease risk are some of the consequences that threaten food security and human well-being. Vulnerable populations in developing nations are often hit hardest, despite contributing the least to global emissions. In conclusion, combating climate change requires urgent collective action from governments, industries, and individuals to ensure a sustainable future for the planet. Education, innovation, and international cooperation will be essential tools in meeting this global challenge.What is the most appropriate synonym for the word “combating” in this context?

दिये गए वाक्य के रेखांकित शब्द का सबसे उपयुक्त पर्यायवाची शब्द चुनिए –  नगर निगम का प्राथमिक कार्य नगरपालिकाओं को आवश्यक सुविधाएँ प्रदान करना है।
मुझे व्यवहारिक ज्ञान नहीं है ।वाक्य के किस अंश में त्रुटि है ?
दिए गए वाक्य के लिए उचित क्रिया चुनकर वाक्य पूर्ण करें-सिक्के _______ हैं।
निम्नलिखित में से किस एक वाक्य में ‘आदान’ विलोम का उचित प्रयोग हुआ है?
options: गंगा को प्रदूषित कौन कर रहा है?
विकास का रास्ता कैसे खुले यह सभी को सोचना है?
पुरस्कार स्वरुप उसने मुझे एक हजार रूपये प्रदान किए ।
आपने मेरी उचित समय पर सहायता की।
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'C' (पुरस्कार स्वरुप उसने मुझे एक हजार रूपये प्रदान किए ।) है।

questions.question: निम्नलिखित वाक्य को गुणवाचक विशेषण द्वारा पूर्ण करें।जो पान तुमने खाया है, वह ____ है।
जल में रहकर मगर से बैर - लोकोक्ति के सही अर्थ का चयन कीजिए।
options: किसी से दुश्मनी नहीं करनी चाहिए
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'C' (आश्रयदाता से बैर असंभव है) है।

questions.question: निम्न मुहावरे का अर्थ बताएं -सही विकल्प का चयन करें -'उल्लू बनाना'

एक सार्थक गद्यांश के निर्माण  हेतु निम्नलिखित वाक्यों का सही क्रम क्या होगा ?A. इनकी तीन रचनाएँ उपलब्ध हैं ।B. इसलिए इन्हें जायसी कहा जाता है ।C. ये अमेठी के निकट जायस के रहने वाले थे ।D. सूफी काव्य परम्परा के श्रेष्ठ कवि मलिक मुहम्मद हैं ।
सही विशेषण को चुनकर वाक्य पूर्ण करें -मेरे पास ____ पेंसिलें हैं।
